info.description:
## Introduction: Propel APIs vs. SFDC

Propel provides coarse-grained REST APIs that address common integration use cases. Endpoints are typically resource-based and accept JSON encoded request payloads and return JSON encoded responses using standard HTTP response codes and authentication mechanisms.

There are two APIs currently available. Both APIs require authentication and all requests are made within the scope of the permissions of the requesting user.

1. Click **Propel APIs**
    
2. Open the **Authorization** tab. The authorization type should be set to OAuth 2.0.
    
3. Click **Get New Access Token**. This opens a browser tab with the Salesforce login screen.
    
4. Log in to your Salesforce org.
    
5. Click **Allow** to grant access to "Propel APIs Collection for Postman" to your org.At this point, if your environment is correctly set up, you should see a success message and you should be redirected to the Postman app.  
    If the redirection doesn't happen, you may need to authorize popups in your browser.  
    Click here for instructions on how to authorize popups.  
    Note: these instructions are for Chrome but the steps should be similar with other browsers.
    
    1. Click the popup error in the address bar, choose to allow popups from Postman:
        
    2. Refresh the page and allow the browser to open the Postman app:
        
6. Copy the value of the `instance_url` field from the token details view. Make sure not to copy the line break character.
    
7. Click **Use Token**.
    
8. Open the **Variables** tab.
    
9. Update the `CURRENT VALUE` of the `endpoint` variable with the value that you just copied from the `instance_url` field in the access token details.
    
10. Click **Save**.

request.description:
Creates one or more new Manufacturer Part records (`PDLM__Manufacturer_Part__c`) in Propel. A Manufacturer Part (MPN) represents a specific part number from a specific manufacturer — it exists independently of any Propel Item and can be associated with multiple Items via their **Manufacturers Tab** (AML). This endpoint is used to pre-populate your manufacturer part library before linking parts to Items.

> 

⚠️ **Legacy endpoint.** This is an older API that predates the Propel v2 API family. For new integrations that need to both create a Manufacturer Part and associate it with an Item in one step, use `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber` instead — it handles Manufacturer Part lookup-or-create and association in a single call.

 
  

**Request Body:**

A JSON array of Manufacturer Part objects. You can create one or multiple parts in a single request.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mfr` | String | **Yes** | The name of an existing Manufacturer (Account) record in Propel. Must match an existing record exactly — an invalid or non-existent manufacturer name will block creation |
| `mpn` | String | **Yes** | The Manufacturer Part Number to assign to the new record |
| `dist` | String | No | The name of an existing Distributor record to associate with this part. If the distributor name is invalid, it is silently ignored (the part is still created without a distributor) |

**Example request body:**

```
jsonCopy code[
  {
    "mfr": "Acme Components",
    "mpn": "ACM-CAP-100NF",
    "dist": "Arrow Electronics"
  },
  {
    "mfr": "Acme Components",
    "mpn": "ACM-RES-10K"
  }
]

 ```

**Response:** Returns `200 OK` with the created Manufacturer Part record(s) on success.

**Watch out for:**

- **`mfr`** **and** **`mpn`** **are both required.** The request will fail if `mfr` is missing. If `mpn` is omitted, the endpoint may still create the record but will auto-generate an MPN from the record ID — which is almost certainly not what you want.
    
- **`mfr`** **must match an existing Manufacturer record exactly.** A non-existent manufacturer name returns an error and blocks creation. A non-existent distributor name (`dist`), however, is silently ignored — the part is created without it, and no error is returned.
    
- **This is an all-or-none operation for bulk requests.** If one part in a multi-item list fails, the entire request is rolled back. No partial creates.
    
- **Duplicate parts are blocked.** You cannot create two Manufacturer Part records with the same `mfr` + `mpn` combination. Adding a distributor (`dist`) to an otherwise identical `mfr` + `mpn` creates a distinct record.
    
- **Extra fields in the request body are silently ignored.** Only `mfr`, `mpn`, and `dist` are processed; any other fields are accepted without error but have no effect.
    
- **Only GET and POST are supported.** PUT, PATCH, and DELETE return `405 Method Not Allowed`.
    

**Related:** To associate an existing Manufacturer Part with an Item, use `GET /services/apexrest/PDLM/ManufacturerPart/?MfrPartId` to look up the record ID first, then use `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber` to link it. To create and associate in one step, use `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber` directly.

request.description:
Retrieves a single Manufacturer Part record (`PDLM__Manufacturer_Part__c`) by its Salesforce record ID. A Manufacturer Part (MPN) in Propel represents a specific part number from a specific manufacturer, independent of which Propel Items it is associated with. This endpoint is useful for looking up an MPN's details — such as its part number, associated manufacturer, and distributor — before associating it with an Item via the **Manufacturers Tab** (AML).

> 

**Legacy endpoint.** This is an older API that predates the Propel v2 API family. For new integrations involving AML (Approved Manufacturer List) data, prefer the `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber` endpoint, which handles Manufacturer Part lookup and association in a single call.

 
  

**Query Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MfrPartId` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID of the Manufacturer Part (`PDLM__Manufacturer_Part__c`) to retrieve |

**Response:** Returns `200 OK` with the Manufacturer Part record data on success, including `mpn` (Manufacturer Part Number), `mfr` (Manufacturer name), and `dist` (Distributor name) fields.

**Error responses:**

- `404 Not Found` — the `MfrPartId` does not match any existing Manufacturer Part record
    

**Watch out for:**

- **This endpoint only supports GET and POST.** PUT, PATCH, and DELETE return `405 Method Not Allowed`.
    
- **`MfrPartId`** **must be a valid Salesforce record ID** — passing an MPN string (the part number itself) instead of the record ID will return a 404 or error. Use SOQL to look up the record ID first if you only have the part number.
    
- **This is a legacy endpoint.** It has limited field support compared to querying `PDLM__Manufacturer_Part__c` directly via the Salesforce REST API, which gives you access to all fields including custom ones.
    

**Related:** To create a new Manufacturer Part via API, use `POST /services/apexrest/PDLM/ManufacturerPart/` (the POST variant of this same endpoint). To associate a Manufacturer Part with an Item, use `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber`.

item.name: Add Manufacturer Parts to an Item

query.description: Item record Id you want to add manufacturer items to

request.description:
Associates one or more existing Manufacturer Parts (MPNs) with a specified Propel Item, adding them to the Item's **Approved Manufacturer List (AML)**. The association is always made on the Item's **draft revision** — if no draft exists, the endpoint automatically creates one before adding the parts.

This endpoint is the programmatic equivalent of adding entries on the **Manufacturers Tab** of an Item in the Propel UI. It is commonly used during CAD/PDM integrations or data migrations to bulk-populate AML data against Propel Items.

> 

⚠️ **Legacy endpoint.** This is an older API that predates the Propel v2 API family. For new integrations, prefer `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber`, which accepts Item Number instead of a Salesforce record ID and is part of the modern, versioned API surface.

 
  

**Query Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemRecordId` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID of the **Item** (`PDLM__Item__c`) to add manufacturer parts to. Must be an Item ID — passing an Item Revision ID or any other object ID returns a `500` error |

**Request Body:**

A JSON object containing an `addAML` array of Manufacturer Part objects to associate with the Item.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mfr` | String | **Yes** | The name of an existing Manufacturer (Account) record in Propel |
| `mpn` | String | **Yes** | The Manufacturer Part Number of the existing Manufacturer Part to associate |
| `dist` | String | No | The Distributor name, used to disambiguate when multiple Manufacturer Parts share the same `mfr` + `mpn` but have different distributors |

**Watch out for:**

- **Both** **`mfr`** **and** **`mpn`** **are required.** Omitting either blocks the association for that entry.
    
- **The Manufacturer Part must already exist in Propel.** This endpoint associates existing parts — it does not create new Manufacturer Part records. Use `POST /services/apexrest/PDLM/ManufacturerPart` first if the MPN doesn't exist yet.
    
- **Omitting** **`dist`** **when duplicates exist adds ALL matching parts.** If multiple Manufacturer Parts share the same `mfr` + `mpn` but differ only by distributor, not specifying `dist` will add all matching variants to the Item — not just the one without a distributor.
    
- **Duplicate parts are blocked.** If a Manufacturer Part is already on the Item's AML, the API will not add it a second time.
    
- **A new draft is auto-created if none exists.** This is a side effect to be aware of in workflows where you don't want an unintended draft created — ensure the Item is in the expected revision state before calling this endpoint.
    
- **`itemRecordId`** **must be an Item ID, not an Item Revision ID.** Passing a `PDLM__Item_Revision__c` ID returns a `500` error.
    
- **This endpoint only supports POST.** All other HTTP methods return `405 Method Not Allowed`.
    

**Related:** To create a net-new Manufacturer Part before associating it, use `POST /services/apexrest/PDLM/ManufacturerPart`. For the modern equivalent of this endpoint, use `PUT /api/v2/aml/:itemNumber`.

item.description:
The AML (Approved Manufacturer List) APIs allow you to create and retrieve Manufacturer Parts, and associate them with Items in Propel. Use these endpoints to manage the list of approved manufacturers and their part numbers for your product catalog.

There are two resource types:

- **Manufacturer Part** — A standalone manufacturer/MPN/distributor record. Use `POST /ManufacturerPart/` to create one or more parts, and `GET /ManufacturerPart/:MfrPartId` to retrieve an existing part by its Salesforce record ID.
    
- **Manufacturer Item** — The association between a Manufacturer Part and an Item. Use `POST /ManufacturerItem/:ItemId` to link one or more Manufacturer Parts to an Item's draft revision.
    

All requests require OAuth 2.0 authentication. The only supported fields in write requests are `manufacturer` (required), `mpn` (required), and `distributor` (optional). All write operations are all-or-none — if any record in a batch fails, no records are created.

request.description: Updates the metadata of an existing Attachment record directly. The target attachment is identified by its Salesforce record ID, passed as the `AttachmentId` query parameter. Unlike the item-number-based endpoint, this call does not upload file content — it updates fields on the `PDLM__Document__c` record only, such as the attachment name and description. No file name matching or revision logic is applied; the record is updated exactly as specified. Returns the updated `PDLM__Document__c` record on success.

request.description: Updates an existing attachment on the specified Item by uploading new file content. The target Item is identified by its item number in the URL path. The attachment to update is matched by **file name** within the Item's revision. Supports two update behaviors: `bump` (default) increments the file's `ContentVersion` by one while preserving the attachment record, or `replace` which deletes the existing attachment and adds the new one. By default, only draft revisions can be updated; pass `updateReleasedRevisions=true` to update released revisions, which requires the Override Business Rules permission. Returns the updated `PDLM__Document__c` record on success.

request.description:
API for managing external document attachments and watermarks. This API is used to link watermarked document records to parent records and item revisions, update system-generated fields, and manage the cleanup of old external files. It's primarily used during document approval workflows when watermarks need to be applied to documents.

Associates an externally processed file with an existing Propel Attachment record and Item Revision. Use this endpoint to write back a file that has been processed outside of Propel — such as a converted or modified document — and link it to the correct Item Revision in your org. On success, returns the updated `PDLM__Document__c` record confirming the associated `ContentDocument` ID, `ContentVersion` ID, Item Revision, and file title.

POST /services/apexrest/PDLM/api/v2/attachment 
{ 
   "itemName": "ITEM-001", 
   "docName": "Technical Drawing.pdf", 
   "description": "Initial design specifications", 
   "versionData": "JVBERi0xLjQKJdPr..." // Base64-encoded file content 
 }

request.description: Adds a new attachment to an existing Propel record — Item, Change Order, or Quality record. Accepts either a base64-encoded file upload or an external URL link. When adding an attachment to an Item whose latest revision is already released, Propel automatically creates a new draft revision and adds the attachment there. If the Item already has a draft revision, the attachment is added directly to it. Returns the newly created `PDLM__Document__c` record on success.

request.description:
Adds an external URL as an attachment on a Propel record — Item, Change Order, or Quality record. Instead of uploading file content, this endpoint links to a document hosted outside of Propel, such as a Google Doc, Confluence page, or any externally accessible URL. The link appears on the **Attachments Tab** of the target record just like a file attachment. When adding a URL attachment to an Item whose latest revision is already released, Propel automatically creates a new draft revision and adds the link there.

**IMPORTANT:** This is the same `POST /v2/attachment` endpoint as **Add Attachment** — the behavior branches based on what's in the request body. When `versionData` (base64 file content) is provided, Propel uploads the file. When no `versionData` is present and only a URL is provided, Propel creates a URL-based attachment record instead. If both are provided, `versionData` takes precedence.

Retrieves the full field-level detail for a specified batch of BOM rows on an Item Revision. The Item Revision is identified by its Record ID in the URL path. The request body contains a list of Assembly Record IDs — obtained from a prior call to **Get BOM Structure** (`GET /v3/bom/{recordId}`) — and returns the complete BOM row data for each one, including quantity, item number, and all fields defined in your BOM Export fieldset.

Because large BOMs can exceed platform limits if retrieved all at once, this endpoint is designed to be called in batches of approximately 200 Assembly IDs at a time. Repeat calls with successive batches until all rows from the structure response have been retrieved.

Unlike `POST /v3/bomtree/{recordId}` — which requires a prior structure call to obtain Assembly IDs — this variant takes the parent Item Revision ID as a query parameter and returns BOM data directly. The `level` parameter limits how many levels deep in the BOM hierarchy to return. The `offset` parameter enables pagination through large BOMs by specifying where in the result set to start.

**IMPORTANT:** This is the SUBSEQUENT response to the Get BOM Row Details.

Most recent request to retrieve subsets of BOM Data for external processing.

Retrieves the full field-level detail for a specific list of Assembly records belonging to the specified Item Revision. The Item Revision is identified by its Record ID via the `revid` query parameter. The request body contains the explicit Assembly Record IDs to fetch, allowing the caller to target a precise subset of BOM rows rather than paging through sequentially.

This is the POST variant of the BOM Slice endpoint, used by Propel's export services (CSV, PDF, BOM export) to fetch BOM data in controlled chunks from an external service (Heroku). The most current implementation is v4. Unlike the GET variant, which pages by row count, this endpoint retrieves only the rows you specify — making it better suited for parallelized or targeted retrieval patterns.

Creates a new Change record of the specified category and optionally adds Affected Items and populates Change detail fields in a single request. The `categoryName` field is required and must match an existing Change category in your org (e.g., `ECO`, `ECR`). Use `itemNames` to specify an array of Item numbers to add as Affected Items — each Item's latest draft revision will be linked to the new Change. Use the `details` object to set values on any standard or custom Change fields at creation time, using either the field label or API name as the key.

itemNames resolves the **latest draft revision** of each Item. An error is returned if no draft exists or if the draft is already on another pending Change.

**Request Body Reference**

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `categoryName` | Yes | Name of the Change category to create (e.g., `"ECO"`) |
| `itemNames` | No | Array of Item numbers to add as Affected Items. Each Item's latest draft revision is used |
| `details` | No | Key-value pairs of Change fields to populate. Accepts field label or API name. For lookup fields, provide a valid Record ID |

request.description:
API for managing Change Order Release Packages (v3). Provides endpoints to retrieve comprehensive release packages containing change order data, affected items, BOMs, attachments, and related information.

The Get Change API (also referred to as the Release Package endpoint) allows you to retrieve comprehensive data about a Change Order and its associated records using a single API call. Rather than making multiple requests to gather Change Order details, affected items, bills of materials, manufacturer parts, attachments, approval history, and more, this endpoint consolidates all of that information into one response.

This endpoint is commonly used for ERP integrations, downstream system synchronization, and data export workflows where a complete picture of a released (or in-progress) Change Order is needed.

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | 2000 | Max number of Affected Items per page |
| `page` | — | Page number for iterating through large Affected Item lists |

Change Affected Items operations. Provides REST endpoint for retrieving all of the affected items related to a change order. Response includes item details, revision details, and task information.

This `POST` endpoint triggers an approval action on the Change Order identified by `:changeId`. Based on the Propel approval model, the four approval actions this class is expected to support are:

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Submit** | Enters the Change into the Salesforce approval process for the current phase |
| **Approve** | Records the calling user's approval for the current approval phase |
| **Reject** | Rejects the current approval phase; triggers auto-reject phase transition if configured |
| **Recall** | Withdraws the Change from the active approval process |

Retrieves a list of Change Orders from your Propel org. Use this endpoint to query multiple Change Orders at once — for example, to identify which Change Orders exist before fetching full release package details for each one using the Get Change (Release Package) V3 endpoint.

This is a collection endpoint, meaning it returns an array of Change Order records rather than a single record with nested related data. It is the programmatic equivalent of viewing the Changes list view in Propel.

**Common use cases:**

- Polling for new or recently updated Change Orders to synchronize with a downstream system (ERP, MES, QMS)
    
- Discovering Change Order IDs or names to use as input for subsequent API calls
    
- Building integration workflows that need to enumerate Change Orders by category or status

request.description:
Grants Collaborator-level access on a Salesforce `ContentDocument` (file/attachment) to a specified user. This endpoint is called internally by Propel's PDF watermarking service to ensure the triggering user — typically the final approver on a Change Order or Item Revision workflow — has the necessary file permissions to complete the watermarking and document supersedure process.

**Why this is needed:**

When a Change Order is approved and Propel's watermarking feature is enabled, the system must update the existing `ContentVersion` of an attachment to apply the watermark and mark the prior revision as superseded. Salesforce requires the user performing that operation to be either the file owner, a System Administrator, or a **Collaborator** on the `ContentDocument`. Because the final approver is often a standard user with only Viewer-level file access, the watermarking process would silently fail or throw an error without this permission being granted first.

This endpoint resolves that by programmatically adding `Collaborator` sharing (`ShareType: C`) to the `ContentDocument` for the relevant user before the watermark and supersedure operation completes.

**Important notes:**

- This endpoint is called by Propel's Heroku-based watermarking service as part of an automated workflow. It is not intended to be called directly by customers or external integrations.
    
- This endpoint is only relevant when the **PDF Watermarking** feature is enabled in your org.
    
- If your org uses **Content Libraries** with restricted access (e.g., a Superseded library), additional configuration may be required. See your Customer Success Manager for guidance.

request.description:
Programmatically import Item, Item Revision, and Bill of Materials (BOM) data into Propel using a base64-encoded CSV payload. This endpoint exposes the same import engine powering the Propel Setup **Import** UI, making it suitable for automated data pipelines, CAD system integrations, and ERP-to-Propel synchronization workflows.

The behavior of the import is controlled by the query parameters in the request URL:

| Parameter | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hasItem` | `true` | The CSV contains Item and Item Revision data |
| `hasBom` | `true` | The CSV contains BOM structure data |
| `hasAML` | `false` | AML (manufacturer part) data is not included |
| `hasATT` | `false` | Attachment data is not included |
| `matchDescription` | `false` | Item matching is by Item Number only, not description |
| `isUpsertingItem` | `true` | Create new Items/Item Revisions or update existing ones (Add & Update) |
| `isUpsertingBOM` | `true` | Add new BOM rows or update existing ones (Add & Update) |
| `isReplacingBOM` | `false` | Do not delete BOM rows absent from the import file |
| `isUpsertingAML` | `false` | Do not process AML rows |
| `isReplacingAML` | `false` | Do not replace AML data |

**Prerequisites:**

- Field mappings must already be configured in your org by running at least one import through the **Propel Setup > Import** UI. The API uses those saved mappings automatically — it cannot define new mappings.
    
- The calling user must have **Salesforce Administrator** privileges.
    
- The request body must be a **base64-encoded string** of a valid, properly formatted CSV file. See [Propel Import Tool: Item Data](https://propelplm.my.site.com/helpcenter/s/article/Propel-Import-Tool-Item-Data) for CSV formatting requirements.
    

**Important:** Always test imports against a Sandbox environment before running against Production. Propel Support does not provide assistance with data migration efforts via this API.

The core Propel Bulk Import endpoint. Accepts a base64-encoded CSV payload and processes it through Propel's import engine — the same engine that powers the **Propel Setup > Import** UI. Use this endpoint to create, update, or replace Items, Item Revisions, BOM structures, Approved Manufacturer List (AML) records, and attachments in bulk via a programmatic integration.

The behavior of the import is controlled entirely by the query parameters you pass in the request URL. All parameters are optional and default to the values shown below if omitted.

**Query Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hasItem` | Boolean | `true` | The CSV contains Item and Item Revision data |
| `hasBom` | Boolean | `true` | The CSV contains BOM structure data |
| `hasAML` | Boolean | `false` | The CSV contains AML (manufacturer part) data |
| `hasATT` | Boolean | `false` | The CSV contains attachment data |
| `matchDescription` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, items are also matched by description in addition to Item Number |
| `isUpsertingItem` | Boolean | `true` | When `true`, create new Items/Item Revisions or update existing ones (Add & Update). When `false`, add new records only |
| `isUpsertingBOM` | Boolean | `true` | When `true`, add new BOM rows or update existing ones (Add & Update) |
| `isReplacingBOM` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, fully replace the BOM — adds, updates, and deletes rows not present in the import file (Add & Update & Delete) |
| `isUpsertingAML` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, add new AML rows or update existing ones |
| `isReplacingAML` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, fully replace the AML — adds, updates, and deletes rows not present in the import file |

**Request Body:**  
The request body must be a raw **base64-encoded string** of a valid, properly formatted CSV file. See [Propel Import Tool: Item Data](https://propelplm.my.site.com/helpcenter/s/article/Propel-Import-Tool-Item-Data) for CSV structure and column requirements.

**Prerequisites:**

- Field column mappings must already be saved in your org by running at least one import through the **Propel Setup > Import** UI. This API uses those saved mappings automatically — it cannot define new column mappings.
    
- The calling user must have **Salesforce Administrator** privileges.
    

**Important:** Always test against a Sandbox environment before running against Production. Propel Support does not provide assistance with data migration via this API. Propel Implementation Services is available for paid assistance.

**Deprecation Notice:** This is the Import V1 Legacy API. Please use Bulk Import (Configurable) or Bulk Import Items & BOMs API. This is limited to files under 5MB.

The primary use of this endpoint is a **GET** (passing a Chatter/ContentDocument file ID in the URL path), while the **POST** variant accepts the CSV as a direct request body.

Accepts a CSV file as the raw POST request body and processes it through Propel's import engine to create or update Items, Item Revisions, and BOM structures. The import behavior is controlled by query parameters appended to the URL.

This endpoint is the POST variant of the v1 Import API, which was introduced to avoid the two-step workflow required by the original GET-based endpoint (which required uploading a file to Salesforce Files first, then passing the resulting ContentDocument ID in the URL).

**Query Parameters** (same set as the v2 endpoint):

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hasItem` | `true` | CSV contains Item/Item Revision data |
| `hasBom` | `true` | CSV contains BOM data |
| `hasAML` | `false` | CSV contains AML data |
| `hasATT` | `false` | CSV contains attachment data |
| `matchDescription` | `false` | Match items by description in addition to Item Number |
| `isUpsertingItem` | `true` | Add & Update items |
| `isUpsertingBOM` | `true` | Add & Update BOM rows |
| `isReplacingBOM` | `false` | Add & Update & Delete BOM rows |
| `isUpsertingAML` | `false` | Add & Update AML rows |
| `isReplacingAML` | `false` | Add & Update & Delete AML rows |

**Limitations:**

- File size is limited to **5 MB**. For larger imports, use `POST /services/apexrest/PDLM/api/v2/import`.
    
- Field column mappings must be pre-configured via at least one import through **Propel Setup > Import**.
    
- Requires **Salesforce Administrator** privileges.

request.description:
Returns a structured redline comparison between a specified Item Revision and its immediately preceding revision, including changes to BOM rows, Attachments, and AML (Approved Manufacturer List) records. This endpoint is the data source powering Propel's **Export PDX** feature and can also be consumed directly by external integrations that need a programmatic diff of what changed between two Item Revisions.

The API compares the provided Item Revision (`itemrevisionId`) against the previous revision in sequence and classifies each changed element with one of four markup types:

| Markup Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Add` | The row exists in the new revision but not the previous one |
| `Delete` | The row existed in the previous revision but was removed in the new revision |
| `Modify` | The row exists in both revisions but one or more field values changed |
| `NoChange` | The row exists in both revisions with no changes |

**What the response includes:**

- **`hasBOMChange`** — Boolean flag indicating whether any BOM rows changed
    
- **`hasAMLChange`** — Boolean flag indicating whether any AML rows changed
    
- **`hasATTChange`** — Boolean flag indicating whether any Attachment rows changed
    
- **`markups`** — Array of markup objects, each containing:
    
    - `sobjectType` — The Salesforce object type of the changed row (e.g., `Assembly__c`, `Manufacturer_Item__c`)
        
    - `markupType` — One of `Add`, `Delete`, `Modify`, or `NoChange`
        
    - `rowOld` — Field values from the **previous** revision
        
    - `rowNew` — Field values from the **current** (given) revision
        
    - `key` — The Item ID used as the comparison key
        

**Path Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `itemrevisionId` | String | The Salesforce record ID (`Id`) of the `PDLM__Item_Revision__c` record to compare against its predecessor |

**Common use cases:**

- Feeding redline markup data into a PDX package for downstream ERP or supply chain systems
    
- Programmatically identifying what BOM or AML changes were made as part of a Change Order
    
- Generating custom change reports or diff summaries in external tools

request.description:
Updates the fields of an existing Item and its active draft Item Revision, identified by Item Number. Pass the Item Number as a query parameter (`?itemNumber=`), and provide a flat JSON key-value payload containing the fields you want to update.

**Key behavior:** When you PUT to a released Item that has no existing draft, the API automatically creates a new draft revision and applies the updates to it. If a draft already exists, the updates are written directly to the existing draft.

**Query Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemNumber` | String | Yes | The Item Number of the Item to update (e.g., `?itemNumber=PCB-00123`) |

**Request Body:**

A flat JSON object of field API name/value pairs. Do **not** nest fields inside a `details` wrapper — the body must be a flat key-value list.

```
jsonCopy code{
  "Description__c": "Updated description",
  "Lifecycle_Phase__c": "Production",
  "Custom_Field__c": "value"
}

 ```

Fields should be provided without the `PDLM__` namespace prefix (e.g., use `Description__c`, not `PDLM__Description__c`).

**Watch out for:**

- **Draft creation:** If the Item has no current draft, this endpoint will create one automatically. This is by design but can be unexpected if you only intended to read the Item — use `GET` in that case.
    
- **Change-Controlled fields:** Fields governed by Change Control Whitelist (CCW) rules are respected. If a field is change-controlled, updating it via this endpoint may be restricted depending on your org's CCW configuration.
    
- **Category changes:** Do not use this endpoint to change an Item's Category to one with a different Lifecycle — this is not supported and will result in an error.
    
- **Released Items:** This endpoint operates on the active draft, not the released revision. To update a released revision directly without creating a draft, use the legacy v1 endpoint (`/Item/`), but note that v1 is not the recommended long-term approach.

request.description:
Creates a new Item and its initial Item Revision in Propel. This is a pure create operation — it always results in a new Item record. To update an existing Item, use `PUT /api/v2/item/?itemNumber` instead.

**Required fields:**

- `category` — The name of a valid, active Propel Category (e.g., `"Capacitor"`, `"Assembly"`, `"Document"`). Category is always required and determines the Lifecycle, autonumbering, and Category-Specific Fields that apply to the Item.
    
- Additional fields may be required depending on your org's **Required Fields** configuration on the Category's first Lifecycle Phase.
    

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | String | **Yes** | The API name or label of the Propel Category to assign to the new Item |
| `name` | String | No | Item Number to assign. If the Category has **Autonumber** configured, the autonumber is used and this field is ignored (unless the calling user has the Override Autonumber custom permission) |
| `details` | Object | No | Key-value pairs of Item Revision field API names and values to set on the initial revision |

**Response:** Returns the newly created Item and Item Revision record data on success (`200 OK`).

**Watch out for:**

- **Autonumber override:** If the Category has **Restrict Autonumber Override** enabled, the `name` field in the request body is ignored — the Item Number will always be generated by the autonumber sequence, regardless of what you pass. Only users with the Override Autonumber custom permission can bypass this.
    
- **Required fields:** If your Category's first Lifecycle Phase has required fields configured, the POST will fail if those fields are not included in `details`. The error response will identify the missing field(s) by both label and API name.
    
- **Concurrent POSTs:** Sending simultaneous POST requests to this endpoint can create multiple separate Item records — this is by design. Unlike `PUT`, there is no idempotency check on `POST /api/v2/item`.
    
- **Default revision:** If `Revision__c` is not included in `details`, the system will generate a default revision value based on the Category's Lifecycle Phase revision sequence.

item.name: Cloned Related Records on Import Draft

request.description:
Triggers an asynchronous batch job that clones related records from a released Item Revision to newly created draft revisions — specifically for drafts created via the Propel **Import** tool. This endpoint bridges a gap between the Import workflow and the **Clone Related Records on Create Draft** feature: when the UI's **Create Draft** action is used, Propel automatically clones configured related records to the new draft; but when a draft is created via Import, the cloning does not happen automatically. Calling this endpoint after an import triggers that same cloning process for the imported drafts.

**When to use this:** Call this endpoint after completing a bulk import that created new Item Revision drafts, if your org has the **Clone related records on Create Draft** setting enabled on any **New FieldSet Mapping** configuration. Without this call, the related records (e.g., junction objects pointing to the previous Item Revision) will not be carried forward to the new drafts.

**How it works:**

1. You run a Propel bulk import that creates one or more new Item Revision drafts
    
2. You POST to this endpoint with the list of newly created Item Revision IDs
    
3. Propel queues the `CloneRelatedObjectBatch` batch job asynchronously
    
4. The batch finds all custom objects configured with **Clone related records on Create Draft** checked in **New FieldSet Mapping**, and clones those related records to point to the new draft revisions

Retrieves a single Item and its active Item Revision by Salesforce record ID or Item Number. This is the primary endpoint for fetching the current state of an Item — its details fields and the fields of the specified (or default) revision — in a single call.

Pass either the Item's Salesforce record ID (e.g., `a000a00000pbMVfAAM`) or its Item Number (e.g., `PCB-00123`) as the path parameter.

**Path Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:Id_or_Name` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID (`PDLM__Item__c`) or the Item Number (Name) of the Item to retrieve |

**Query Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `revision` | String | No | Latest Released | The revision name or revision record ID to return. If no released revision exists, defaults to the latest draft revision |
| `nestedAttachments` | Boolean | No | `false` | When `true`, returns attachments from all Items on the Item's BOM, not just the top-level Item |

**Response:** Returns the Item record fields and the matching Item Revision fields as a single JSON object. The response shape mirrors the data visible on the **Details Tab** of the Item record in Propel.

Updates Item Revision fields on an existing Item by Salesforce record ID or Item Number. If the Item has an existing draft revision, the draft is updated. If the Item has only a released revision (no draft), **a new draft revision is automatically created** with the specified field values applied to it.

This is the primary endpoint for programmatically writing field values back to an Item Revision — used in CAD integration, ERP synchronization, and data enrichment workflows.

**Path Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:Id_or_Name` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID (`PDLM__Item__c`) or the Item Number (Name) of the Item to update |

**Watch out for:**

- **Flat body required:** Do not nest fields inside a `details` object. The body must be a flat key-value JSON object. A nested request body will return a `200 OK` but silently fail to update any fields.
    
- **Auto-creates a draft:** If the Item has no existing draft, this endpoint creates a new draft revision before applying the field updates. This is intentional behavior — but be aware it will increment your revision state if you weren't expecting it.
    
- **CCW (Change Control Whitelist) fields:** If fields in your org are protected by the Change Control Whitelist feature, updating those fields via this endpoint may behave unexpectedly — creating a new draft rather than updating the released revision in-place. This is a known open issue (MVP-27847) as of early 2026. Verify CCW field behavior in your org before relying on this endpoint for CCW-protected fields.
    
- **Field API names without namespace:** Pass field API names without the `PDLM__` namespace prefix (e.g., use `Description__c`, not `PDLM__Description__c`).
    
- **Simultaneous PUT requests:** Unlike POST, simultaneous PUT requests to the same Item Number are idempotent — only one draft will be created, and subsequent requests will update the existing draft.

Retrieves the attachment metadata for a specified Item and Item Revision. This endpoint returns the `ContentVersion` IDs and associated file information for all attachments on the Item — it does **not** return the binary file content. A separate Salesforce API call using the returned `ContentVersion` ID is required to download the actual file.

This endpoint is commonly used in document management integrations, CAD/PDM synchronization workflows, and downstream systems that need to locate and pull the latest released drawings or documents associated with a Propel Item.

**Path Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:itemId` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID or Item Number of the Item whose attachments you want to retrieve |

**Query Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `revision` | String | No | Latest Released | The revision name or revision record ID to retrieve attachments for. If the Item has no released revision, defaults to the latest draft |
| `nestedAttachments` | Boolean | No | `false` | When `true`, returns attachments from **all Items on the BOM**, not just the top-level Item. Useful for retrieving all drawings associated with an assembly and its components in a single call |

**Response:** Returns an array of attachment records with `ContentVersion` IDs and file metadata (file name, size, type, etc.). Use the `ContentVersion` ID in a subsequent call to the Salesforce Content API (`/services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/ContentVersion/:id/VersionData`) to download the binary file content.

**Watch out for:**

- **This endpoint returns metadata only — not files.** You must make a second API call to the Salesforce `ContentVersion` object to download actual file content. Do not expect a binary response from this endpoint.
    
- **Duplicate attachments with** **`nestedAttachments=true`****:** If multiple Items on a BOM share the same attachment, the same `ContentVersion` ID may appear more than once in the response. Deduplicate by `ContentVersion` ID before downloading.
    
- **Revision name collisions:** If multiple Item Revisions share the same revision name (e.g., two drafts both named `A\*`), specify a revision record ID instead of a name to guarantee the correct revision is targeted.
    
- **Draft revisions:** By default, the endpoint targets the latest _released_ revision. If the Item has only a draft and no released revision, the draft is returned instead.
    

**Related:** To upload or update attachments on an Item, use `PUT /api/v2/attachment/:itemNumber`. To retrieve attachment metadata as part of a Change Order release package, use `GET /api/v3/change/:changeId?attachments=true`.

Triggers an asynchronous export of a Trace Matrix CSV file for a specified Item. This is the API equivalent of clicking the **Export CSV** button on the **Trace Matrix** record page in Propel. Rather than returning the file directly, the endpoint queues the export job and delivers the resulting CSV file as a Chatter post on both the Trace Matrix record and the calling user's Chatter feed.

The Trace Matrix CSV captures the full traceability state of the Item — including all linked Requirements, User Needs, Test Plans, Requirement Outputs, and BOM-level traceability — at the moment the export is triggered. It is the primary artifact for demonstrating design control traceability in regulated product development environments (e.g., FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485).

**Query / Path Parameter:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `recordId` | String | Yes | The Salesforce record ID of the **Item** (`PDLM__Item__c`) for which the Trace Matrix export should be triggered |

**Response:** Returns `200 OK` with an `"Export request received"` message immediately. The export runs asynchronously — the CSV file will appear in the **Chatter** feed of both the associated Trace Matrix record and the calling user's profile page once processing completes. There is no binary file in the response body.

**Exported file naming convention:** `[Item Name] Trace Matrix [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS]`

**Watch out for:**

- **This is an asynchronous trigger, not a file download.** The `200 OK` response confirms the export was queued, not that the file is ready. You must poll Chatter or monitor the Trace Matrix record to retrieve the file after the job completes.
    
- **`feature.requirements`** **must be enabled.** If the Requirements feature is disabled in your org (`feature.requirements = false`), the API returns a `500` error. Confirm the feature flag is active before calling this endpoint.
    
- **The calling user must have the Propel Requirement Full Use permission set** to export Trace Matrix data. Users without this permission will see an error in Chatter rather than a completed export.
    
- **Items with no Requirements** will still return `200 OK` and produce an export — but the CSV file will be empty (containing only the column header template). The file is still posted to the calling user's Chatter.
    
- **This endpoint only supports GET and HEAD.** POST, PUT, and DELETE return `405 Method Not Allowed`.

request.description:
Creates an MBOM header, its first branch, the branch's eBOM source lineage, and that source's first acceptance — **four records in one transaction, and zero rows of BOM structure**.

All four ids come back rather than just `mbomId`, because a caller that had to go looking for the other three would be querying schema this API exists to hide. The one you will use most is **`branchSourceCiId`** — that is the `sourceId` every `/sources/...` endpoint takes.

## Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rootItemRevisionId` | Id | **Yes** | The **Released** `Item_Revision__c` the MBOM is built over. Its `Released_Date_Time__c` becomes **T_R**. |
| `mbomName` | String(80) | **Yes** | `MBOM__c.Name`. |
| `branchLabel` | String(80) | **Yes** | Lands on **both** `Branch__c.Name` and `Branch__c.Label__c`. |

## The root revision must be Released

T_R is the root revision's release date, and an unreleased revision has no such date — the pin has nothing to pin to. Four shapes are refused with `NOT_RELEASED`:

- not released;
- **Cancelled**;
- **Expired**;
- released but carrying no release date.

Cancelled and Expired are excluded because the eBOM's own as-of read would never resolve them either — pinning an MBOM to one means pinning it to a revision upstream considers withdrawn.

> **Why 409 and not 400.** The request is well formed. Releasing the revision makes the *identical* request succeed, which is exactly what 409 means in this API.

## Two timestamps, both stamped here

| Field | Value | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Source_TimePoint__c` (**T_R**) | the root revision's release date | what inherited rows resolve at, forever |
| `Accepted_At__c` | the **wall clock**, now | which acceptance governs a given `asOf` |

Setting T_R to `now` is the single change that would silently turn a pinned MBOM into a floating one — and every row would still render, so nothing would look wrong.

## Watch out for

- **Because `Accepted_At__c` is the wall clock, a branch created now renders nothing when read at an `asOf` in the past.** That is the acceptance not existing yet at that timestamp, not a defect. It surprises everyone once.
- **A blank `mbomName` is refused, deliberately.** A custom object's Text `Name` is unenforced by the API, so a blank one would silently produce an MBOM named after its own record id that nobody can search for.
- **A malformed id in the *body* is a 400, while one in the *URI* is a 404.** Not an inconsistency: the URI is what *names* the resource, so a path naming nothing is a path to nothing. A body field is a value in a request to a resource that does exist.
- **Unknown JSON keys are silently ignored.** So a *mistyped* field name reads as a null value — `rootItemRevisionld` with a lowercase L answers `NOT_FOUND`, not a schema error.

## Access

Gated **before the body is read**: a caller with no create grant gets 403 whatever they sent, rather than also being told their JSON was malformed for an action they were never permitted to attempt.

Requires **create** on `MBOM__c`, `Branch__c`, `Branch_Source_CI__c`, `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c`, and **read** on `Item_Revision__c`. All five are named so a partial grant is a clean 403 rather than a 500 out of the middle of the DML.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Unreadable body; blank or over-length `mbomName` / `branchLabel` |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Missing create on any of the four objects, or read on `Item_Revision__c` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | `rootItemRevisionId` is null, not an `Item_Revision__c`, or names no visible row |
| 409 | `NOT_RELEASED` | Root revision unreleased, Cancelled, Expired, or missing a release date |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

request.description:
The branch's resolved content at one timepoint: the eBOM traversed at **T_R**, with the branch's own deltas folded and overlaid at **`asOf`**.

This is the main read, and it is where the two-clock model becomes visible — every row states its own `provenance` and its own `governingTimestamp`, because a row that did not carry its own clock would be unexplainable to the person looking at it.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branchId` | Id | **Yes** | The `Branch__c`. A malformed id, or a well-formed id of the *wrong object*, is a **404** — which is why swapping a `branchId` for a `sourceId` is a clean 404 rather than a 500 out of a repository. |

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flat` | Boolean | No | `true` | Response shape. Only an explicit `false` nests. |
| `asOf` | ISO-8601 | No | now | The branch clock. Never accepted in the future. |

### `asOf` parsing

Accepts ISO-8601 (`2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`, `2026-02-01T00:00:00+05:30`) and the space-separated Apex form (`2026-02-01 03:04:05`, read as GMT). A `+` offset is **repaired server-side** after query-string decoding turns it into a space — so a perfectly legal ISO offset does not fail for a fault that happened in transport.

## Response fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `asOf` | Echoed, so the response is self-describing — present even when you sent none |
| `rootRevisionId` | The root `Item_Revision__c` the structure hangs from |
| `sourceTimePoint` | **T_R** — what inherited rows are pinned at |
| `rows[]` | Always present; empty rather than absent |
| `warnings[]` | Always present; empty rather than absent |

### Per-row fields worth understanding

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `provenance` | `inherited` / `claimed` / `local`. Derived at read time, never stored |
| `governingTimestamp` | T_R for an inherited row, `asOf` for a local or substituted one |
| `edgeId` | **Null for a purely inherited row** — no branch-owned record exists until something claims it |
| `edgeKey` | The legacy `Assembly__c` line id, or a synthetic `local-…` / `replaces-…` key for branch content |
| `isExcluded` | **Rendered, not filtered.** A tree read shows the editor what was removed. (A *baseline* read filters them out.) |
| `isEditable` | **False** inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly. Every delta op refuses those rows, so a UI offering an action on one is offering an action the API will reject |
| `isReplaced` | True when this row stands in for another |
| `childRows` | Populated in the nested shape only; **empty, never null**, in the flat shape |

## Watch out for

- **The nested shape duplicates a shared subassembly; the flat shape does not.** The traversal walks a DAG and emits a shared subtree once; nesting re-materialises it under every parent that uses it, because that is what a BOM tree looks like to a person expanding it. So the two shapes carry the same *content* but not the same row **count** — never treat a nested row count as a total — and a deeply shared DAG can hit heap nested while rendering comfortably flat.
- **A flat response is losslessly re-nestable.** Every row carries `parentItemId`, in both shapes.
- **Unreachable rows are dropped, from both shapes.** A delta can name a parent item that is not in the tree — a subassembly whose item had nothing released at T_R drops out, and a claim beneath it would otherwise survive as a row with an absent parent.
- **`flat=0` and `flat=no` mean flat, not nested.** `Boolean.valueOf('0')` is `false`, so the obvious implementation would *nest* for `flat=0` — the opposite of what that caller asked for. Unrecognised values fall back to flat rather than raising, because a flat response loses nothing.
- **A branch created today renders nothing at a past `asOf`.** Its acceptance did not exist yet at that timestamp.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `ASOF_INVALID` | `asOf` could not be parsed |
| 400 | `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` | `asOf` is later than now |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | No read on `Branch__c` (or a field-level denial deeper in the stack) |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The id is absent, unparseable, names another object, or the path has an unrecognised trailing segment |
| 422 | `EBOM_CYCLE` | The source eBOM itself contains a cycle. Fix the eBOM; retrying is pointless |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

request.description:
The **"what would I inherit?"** read: the structure as one source supplies it, with the branch's claims, excludes and replaces deliberately **not** overlaid.

Use it to answer *"what did I change relative to upstream?"* by diffing this against the branch tree read. Every row comes back `provenance: inherited`.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceId` | Id | **Yes** | The `Branch_Source_CI__c`. In Phase 1 a branch has exactly one source, of `Source_Type__c = Ebom`. |

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asOf` | ISO-8601 | No | now | Which accepted source version governs |

## Why there is no `flat` parameter

A source's own structure has no deltas overlaid on it, so there is no nesting decision to make. An unexpected `flat` is **ignored rather than rejected**, so one parameter set can be sent to both tree reads without branching in the client.

## Watch out for

- **There is no `branchId` in this path**, and there does not need to be: the source already names its owning branch through `Branch_Source_CI__c.Downstream_Branch__c`.
- **This read does not tell you what the branch renders.** An excluded row still appears here, because the source still supplies it — exclusion is the *branch's* assertion, not the source's.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `ASOF_INVALID` / `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` | See the branch tree read |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | No read on `Branch_Source_CI__c` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The id is absent, unparseable, or names another object |
| 422 | `EBOM_CYCLE` | The source eBOM contains a cycle |

request.description:
Takes one live eBOM line into the branch as a **copy-on-write override**, so the branch can diverge from it. This is the operation everything else depends on: an inherited row is read-only until it is claimed.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ebomAssemblyId` | **Yes** | The legacy `Assembly__c` line being claimed |
| `clientRef` | No | Your token, echoed on the result |

## What it writes — five records

| Record | Carries |
| --- | --- |
| `Assembly_CI__c` | edge **identity**, keyed on the eBOM line via `Edge_Key__c` |
| `CI__c` | the 1:1 wrapper the delta log points at |
| `Assembly_CI_Rev__c` | the values, **copied as they stood at claim time** |
| `CI_Rev__c` | the branch-scoped revision owning those values |
| `Branch_Member__c` | membership, with `Overrides_Source__c` set |

That last field is what makes this a *claim* rather than an *add*: provenance is derived from it, so a claim that forgot it would produce a row rendering as branch-local content that never came from the eBOM — and "what did I change relative to upstream?" would stop being answerable.

## Identity is the eBOM **line**, never the (parent, child) pair

An eBOM legitimately carries two lines for one pair — two of the same screw at different find numbers. Keying on the pair would collapse them into one edge. `Edge_Key__c` holds the `Assembly__c` line id and is a unique External Id, which is also what makes two writers racing on one line collide in the database rather than both succeeding.

## The parent is stored as an **item**, not a revision

The parent revision moves whenever a newer source is accepted, and an edge stored against it would be orphaned by that acceptance. There is a second and stronger reason: `Edge_Key__c` is unique **org-wide**, so two branches claiming the same eBOM line share **one** `Assembly_CI__c` row — meaning every field on that row must be branch-*invariant*. A parent revision derived from the resolving branch is not.

## Watch out for

- **Two claims of one line in a single batch** — the second is refused `ALREADY_CLAIMED`, exactly as it would be in a later batch, even though the pre-batch snapshot shows the line as still inherited.
- **A past `asOf` is refused.** Claiming mints a new identity, and an identity cannot be validated against a stale view.
- **Claiming does not change any value.** It copies what is already there. Change it with `update` — in a *separate request*.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No `ebomAssemblyId`, or a past `asOf` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The line is not in this branch's structure |
| 409 | `ALREADY_CLAIMED` | This branch already owns the row |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | The row is inside a locally added or substituted assembly |

item.name: update — revise quantity or find number

request.description:
Revises the quantity and find number of a **branch-owned** edge.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assemblyCiId` | one of | An existing `Assembly_CI__c` edge — the ordinary form |
| `ebomAssemblyId` | one of | The legacy line. **Accepted deliberately**, and it has to be: an inherited row has no edge record, so this is the only id a client holds for the row whose update must come back `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Without it that rejection could never be reached |
| `quantity` | | New quantity |
| `findNumber` | | New find number |

## Copy-on-write revisions

The current `CI_Rev__c` is edited **in place** while it is `Draft`. Otherwise a new revision is allocated (`Revision_Number__c + 1`, with the current one recorded as its predecessor), the current one is **frozen**, and `forked` comes back **`true`**.

That is what makes `Revision_Number__c` mean *"number of checkpoints"* rather than *"number of times someone pressed save"*.

> In practice: **updates fork once a baseline has been cut**, because cutting a baseline freezes every revision it resolved to. Before that, they revise in place.

### In-place is not a rewrite of history

An in-place revise *does* change what a read at an earlier `asOf` returns, and that is the design rather than a hole in it. A `Draft` revision is one nothing depends on yet. The append-only rule governs **membership**, which `update` never touches — and the moment anything does depend on a revision, it freezes and every later revise forks.

## Membership is not touched

No `Branch_Member__c` row, either way. The CI is already a member and revising its payload does not change that; appending one anyway would put a membership act in the log for a membership that never moved.

## Watch out for

- **An inherited edge is refused, never silently claimed.** `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, carrying the eBOM line so the client can offer the claim. An update that quietly claimed would make "what did I change relative to the eBOM?" depend on which fields a user happened to touch.
- **`claim` then `update` in one batch fails.** Both validate against the same pre-batch snapshot, so the update still sees an inherited row. Two requests.
- **`STALE_REVISION`, not a fork, under a past `asOf`.** If your view is stale enough that the revision already has a descendant, forking would write revision N+1 a second time and lose the newer content.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No id supplied, or nothing to change |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The edge is not in this branch |
| 409 | `CLAIM_REQUIRED` | The row is inherited |
| 409 | `NOT_SUPPLIED` | The branch holds no content for the row |
| 409 | `STALE_REVISION` | Your view is behind |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Nested inside a local or substituted assembly |

item.name: add — a part the eBOM never supplied

request.description:
Adds a part to the branch that the eBOM **never supplied** — packaging, fixtures, consumables, process aids. This is the classic manufacturing-vs-engineering difference.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parentItemId` | **Yes** | The parent **item** (never a revision) — must be part of this configuration |
| `childItemId` | **Yes** | The part being added |
| `quantity` | **Yes** | |
| `findNumber` | **Yes** | |

## Branch-**local**: one field is the whole difference

`add` and `claim` write the same five records and differ in exactly one: `Overrides_Source__c` is **null** here. Setting it would make a part that never came from the eBOM claim to be an override of it.

The edge key is synthetic — `local-{branchId}-{parentItemId}-{childItemId}` — because no legacy line exists to point at.

## Local content floats

A local edge never came through a source, so it has no T_R to pin to: **its child resolves to whatever is released at `asOf`**. It is also invisible before the moment it was created, which falls out of the effective-date stamp rather than needing a rule of its own.

This is one of the two ways a `MIXED_REVISION` warning appears.

## Watch out for

- **One local part cannot appear twice under one parent this phase.** The key is derived from the (parent, child) pair, so a second add is `ALREADY_PRESENT`, pointing at `update`. Note the asymmetry: an eBOM legitimately *can* carry two lines for one pair.
- **Everything beneath a locally added assembly is read-only.** Rows in its subtree come back `isEditable: false` and every delta op refuses them.
- **Cycles are checked against the batch, not just the snapshot.** Two adds can jointly close a loop that neither closes alone — `[add(A,B), add(B,A)]` over a tree with `root→A` and `root→B` — so the walk also reads what this batch has already accepted.
- **A past `asOf` is refused.** Adding mints a new identity.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Missing a required field, or a past `asOf` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | `childItemId` names no item |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | The branch already adds that part under that parent |
| 409 | `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | The pair exists locally but is tombstoned — `restore` it |
| 422 | `PARENT_NOT_IN_BRANCH` | The parent is not part of this configuration |
| 422 | `CYCLE_DETECTED` | The edge would make the child an ancestor of its own parent |

request.description:
Removes a row from this configuration **without deleting anything**. This is how the MBOM says "engineering ships this, manufacturing does not consume it".

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ebomAssemblyId` | one of | The legacy line — the only id you hold for a row not yet claimed |
| `ciId` | one of | An existing `CI__c` |

## One delta row, and **no cascade**

Excluding a subassembly orphans everything beneath it, and **none of that is written**. The descendant prune is computed **at read time**, because a descendant still supplied through another path must survive — and only a read knows the whole graph.

Writing cascade rows would also have to be undone by `restore`, one row at a time, against a graph that may have changed in between.

## An unclaimed row gets a stub, and the stub carries **no revision**

A marker needs somewhere to hang, so excluding an inherited row mints the edge identity and its wrapper — and deliberately **no payload and no revision**. A tombstone asserts an *absence*; giving it content would make it assert a row.

## Nothing is deleted

The delta is appended with the wall clock, so a read at any earlier timepoint still resolves the row as present. A hard delete of any branch-owned row is refused outright and points you here.

## Watch out for

- **The row still appears in the branch tree read**, carrying `isExcluded: true`, so the person editing can see what was removed. It is filtered out of a *baseline* read, which is the record of what the branch contained.
- **A replaced row is already excluded** — its substitution is what stands in for it. Restoring it would put *both* parts in the configuration.
- **Excluding an unclaimed row refuses a past `asOf`**, because it mints an identity. Excluding a row that already has a CI does not.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No id, or a past `asOf` on a minting exclusion |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The row is not in this branch |
| 409 | `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | It already carries a tombstone |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Nested inside a local or substituted assembly |

request.description:
Lifts an exclusion, returning the row to whatever it was before it.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ciId` | **Yes** | The `CI__c`. **`ebomAssemblyId` is not accepted** — by the time a row can be restored it necessarily has a CI |

## Two delta types, decided by what the branch holds

A restore does **not** always re-assert the row, and doing so blindly would break the next read:

| The branch has… | What is appended | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a payload (the row was claimed or added before being excluded) | **`Add`** | re-asserts the branch's own content |
| none (an inherited row excluded straight from a stub) | **`Revert`** | drops the branch's assertion entirely; the row falls back to inheritance |

A tombstone carries no payload, so an `Add` that resolves to nothing is corruption — hence the split.

> Restoring an inherited row **is** falling back to the source, so this is the same act `revert` performs, reached from the other direction.

## Watch out for

- **A past `asOf` is refused.** The Add-vs-Revert choice is read off what the branch holds **now**. A stale snapshot answers it wrongly in the one direction that loses content: filtering out a revision written after that timepoint makes a claimed row look payload-free, so `Revert` is appended and the branch's own content is dropped.
- **A replaced row is not simply an excluded one.** A substitution excludes the row it supersedes, so a replaced row *looks* excluded to this operation — and restoring it would put **both** parts in the configuration, because lifting the exclusion does not remove the substitute. It is refused `ALREADY_PRESENT`; exclude the substitute first.
- **Nothing is rewritten.** One row appended at the next sequence. The exclusion stays in the log, so a read at a timepoint between the two still resolves the row as excluded — which is what makes a baseline cut in that window reproducible.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No `ciId`, or a past `asOf` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The row is not in this branch |
| 409 | `NO_OVERRIDE` | It is not excluded |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | It was **replaced**, not simply excluded |

request.description:
Substitutes a different child for the one an eBOM line supplies — an alternate motor, a second-source connector — **while recording that it is a substitution**.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replacedEbomAssemblyId` | **Yes** | The legacy line being superseded |
| `newChildItemId` | **Yes** | The substitute part |
| `quantity` | **Yes** | |
| `findNumber` | **Yes** | |

## Two units, and the substitution link is the whole point

| Unit | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | tombstones the superseded row — minting its stub first if it was unclaimed |
| 2 | the substitute: edge, wrapper, payload, Draft revision, membership |

Writing it as *just* an exclusion plus an addition would be wrong: the pair would read as an unrelated removal and an unrelated addition, and nothing downstream could say what this part is standing in for. `Assembly_CI__c.Replaces__c` carries the link, and `isReplaced` on a tree row is derived from it.

The superseded row's subtree disappears with it, and none of that is written — the orphan prune is read-time, exactly as for a plain `exclude`.

## The substitute's child **floats**

Its revision is left unpinned and resolves at the read clock. A substitute is branch-chosen content that never came through the source, so it has no T_R to pin to — pinning it would freeze it at whatever happened to be released the moment somebody chose the part.

**`Overrides_Source__c` is still set**, though, and that is not a contradiction: the row overrides something the source supplies, so its provenance is `claimed` rather than `local`. What floats is the *revision*, not the *lineage*.

## Watch out for

- **Only an eBOM-derived row can be replaced.** A branch-**local** row has a synthetic `local-…` key and no `Assembly__c` line. Replacing local content is `update`, or `exclude` plus `add`.
- **One substitution per row.** A second `replace` on a row that already has one is refused — and refused *before* the "already excluded" check, because a replaced row is excluded by its own substitution, and that answer would send you to `restore`, which brings the original back **alongside** the substitute.
- **Swapping one substitute for another is supported**: exclude the live substitute, then replace the row again with a different part.
- **Everything beneath a substituted assembly is read-only** (`isEditable: false`), same as for a local add.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Missing a required field, or a past `asOf` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The superseded line is not in this branch |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | The row already has a live substitute, or the substitute pair already exists |
| 409 | `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | The row is excluded by something **other** than a substitution |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Nested inside a local or substituted assembly |
| 422 | `CYCLE_DETECTED` | The substitute would close a loop |

request.description:
Discards the branch's override of a row, so it falls back to whatever its source supplies. The "**discard my change**" action.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ciId` | one of | The `CI__c` |
| `ebomAssemblyId` | one of | The legacy line. **Accepted deliberately**: a reverted row renders with no `CI__c` at all, so a *second* revert — which must answer `NO_OVERRIDE` — cannot be addressed any other way |

## Nothing on disk is touched

Discarding an override cannot mean **deleting** the branch's records (a later re-claim has to continue from them) and it cannot mean leaving a row with no content. Every shape that *mutates* loses one of the two.

So a `Revert` marker is appended, and the fold drops a `Revert` winner from the resolution entirely — the row resolves exactly as if the branch had never spoken about it, and every record stays where it was.

Because membership is append-only, a read dated **before** the revert still returns the override, which is what keeps a baseline cut in that window reproducible.

## `revert` is not `restore`, and the two meet in the middle

`restore` appends a `Revert` for precisely the row that has no branch payload. This is that act reached from the other direction — which is also why **reverting an excluded row lifts the exclusion**: an exclusion is an override too.

## The three refusals, in the order their remedies work

Every guard answers from the one pre-batch snapshot, so when two are true at once the **order** decides what you are told and therefore what you do next:

1. **`NO_OVERRIDE`** — the branch asserts nothing about this row.
2. **`ALREADY_PRESENT`** — the row was **replaced**. Reverting it drops its exclusion while the substitute stays live, putting both parts in the configuration. The remedy is about the substitute.
3. **`NOT_SUPPLIED`** — no source supplies this row, so falling back would make it **vanish**. That is a delete wearing another name; `exclude` is the operation that means it.

## Watch out for

- **A claimed row whose eBOM line has since disappeared upstream is *not* refused.** Reverting it does make it vanish, and that is correct: the source now supplies nothing there, and "fall back to the source" is exactly what was asked.
- **A past `asOf` is refused.** Every guard above is a statement about what the branch holds *now*, while the appended marker discards its assertions whatever the snapshot's age. A stale view passes the substitute guard without seeing the substitute, and both parts of a replacement then leave the configuration.

## Errors specific to this op

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No id, or a past `asOf` |
| 409 | `NO_OVERRIDE` | The branch asserts nothing about this row |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | The row was replaced |
| 409 | `NOT_SUPPLIED` | No source supplies it — use `exclude` |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Nested inside a local or substituted assembly |

request.description:
Severs a claimed edge's link to the source it overrides, so it stops being a copy-on-write override of upstream content and becomes **branch-owned content in its own right** — retaining exactly the quantity, child revision and row it already has.

This is the same operation the pull commit endpoint runs for a `convert-to-native` disposition.

## Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ciId` | **Yes** | The `CI__c` of the claimed edge |

## An appended assertion, not a rewritten row

Provenance lives on the append-only delta log, so this "severs" the same way `revert` "discards": by appending a new membership row at the next sequence with **no source named**, which wins the fold and reads as `local` provenance from here on.

The CI, its revision and its payload are **untouched** — nothing about the content changes, only what the branch asserts about where it came from.

A read dated before this op still resolves the row as `claimed`, which is what makes a baseline cut in that window reproducible.

## Why you would do this

It is the answer to *"upstream removed this line, but manufacturing still needs the part."* The pull commit endpoint offers it as one of the two dispositions for an `override-orphaned` entry.

## Watch out for

- **This is what triggers `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT`.** A baseline cut *before* the conversion re-resolves with the same row count, the same quantities and the same revisions — but a different `claimed` count. That second canary exists precisely because the first one cannot see this.
- **A past `asOf` is refused.** Every guard reads the branch's *current* provenance.
- **A replaced row is refused before the excluded check.** A replaced row is excluded by its own substitution, so asking "is it excluded?" first would misreport it as `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` and send you after a remedy ("there is no content to retain") that is not true — content survives, on the substitute.

## Errors specific to this op

| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | No `ciId`, or a past `asOf` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The row is not in this branch |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | The row was replaced — convert its substitute instead |
| 409 | `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | A tombstone carries no content to retain |
| 409 | `NO_OVERRIDE` | The row is already branch-native |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Nested inside a local or substituted assembly |
