item.description:
**Every request in this folder is the same endpoint**: `POST /v4/mbom/branches/:branchId/deltas`. They differ only in the `op` inside the body. They are split out one per operation so each can be documented and demonstrated on its own; in real use you send several in one `operations[]` array.

---

# How a batch executes

1. **Size check.** More than 200 operations is `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before anything is resolved — an oversized batch is rejected for free rather than after a full traversal it was never going to be allowed to use.
2. **One snapshot.** The branch is resolved **once**, at `asOf`. That is the whole reason a batch endpoint exists: twenty operations resolving the branch each would be twenty traversals, and the tree could shift underneath the batch halfway through.
3. **Validate everything, then apply.** Two passes, never interleaved, so **every** fault is reported rather than only the first.
4. **Persist** in a fixed number of DML statements — twenty claims cost the same statements as one.

## Order is preserved, but order is not sequencing

Results come back in request order with your `clientRef` echoed and `index` stated. But **every operation validates against the one pre-batch snapshot, so a later operation cannot see an earlier one's effect.**

`[claim(L), update(L)]` in one batch answers `CLAIM_REQUIRED` on the update — and under the default `atomic: true` that rejects the whole batch.

> **Dependent edits are two requests, not two operations.**

## `atomic` — the failure contract is yours to choose

| `atomic` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `true` (**default** — a null wins the safer contract) | All-or-nothing. Any validation failure throws: the status is the **first failure's own code** (so a batch whose only fault is `CLAIM_REQUIRED` still answers 409, not a generic 400) and the body carries a `failures[]` array with **every** failure. The branch is left exactly as it was. |
| `false` | Apply what is valid, report the rest. **`200`** with per-operation `results[]` — check `failed` and each `results[].success`, not the status code. |

`atomic: false` reports per-operation **validation** failures only. It does not fall back to per-operation DML: the aggregate is one savepoint and one set of statements, and a failure there rolls the batch back and propagates.

## `asOf` chooses what a batch *validates* against; it never dates the write

Every row written is effective **now**, whatever `asOf` says. A past `asOf` means *"validate against the configuration as it stood then"* — optimistic concurrency, not time travel. Backdating the write would let a batch win the current fold **and** change what a read at an intervening timestamp returned, rewriting history in an append-only log — and immutable history is what baselines rest on.

Several operations therefore **refuse a past `asOf` outright** with `INVALID_REQUEST`, because they decide from the branch's *current* state: `restore`, `revert`, `convert-to-native`, and any `claim` / `add` / `exclude` / `replace` that has to mint a new edge identity.

## `Idempotency-Key`

Read and passed through, and **ignored this phase**. It is accepted so a client can start sending it now without its first request failing, and a later phase can honour it without a breaking change.

## Why 200 and not 201

Rows *are* created, but the response is a **report** on a set of operations, not a pointer to one new resource — and under `atomic: false` some of them may have failed. A 201 would claim more than happened.

---

# Result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `index` | Zero-based position in the request. Stated because correlating on order alone breaks the moment anything is reordered |
| `clientRef` | Your own token, echoed verbatim. Null when you set none — which is why `index` is stated too |
| `success` | |
| `errorCode` | An error-code name on failure. **Note the key is `errorCode` here, inside a per-operation result** — the top-level *error body* uses `code` |
| `ciId` / `assemblyCiId` | The records this operation created or acted on |
| `forked` | See below |

## `forked` is tri-state, on purpose

Only `update` can fork. So:

- `true` — the update had to allocate a **new** `CI_Rev__c` because a baseline had frozen the current one. Surfaced because your next read will show a revision number you did not ask for.
- `false` — this write **could** have forked and did not.
- `null` — **not applicable.** There was nothing to fork on a `claim` or an `exclude`, and a defaulted `false` would assert "no fork happened" about an operation for which the question is meaningless.

A client must treat `false` and `null` differently, so the field has to be able to say both.

---

# Access

Requires **create** on `Assembly_CI__c`, `CI__c`, `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, `CI_Rev__c` and `Branch_Member__c`, **and edit** on `Assembly_CI__c` (upserted) and `CI_Rev__c` (updated when an operation freezes a predecessor).

Create and edit are not the same permission, and both are named so a partial grant is a 403 **before any DML** rather than a 500 half way through it.

# Shared error responses

| Status | code | Cause | Remedy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Unreadable body; missing required field; unknown `op`; an op that refuses a past `asOf` | Fix the request |
| 400 | `ASOF_INVALID` / `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` | The batch's own `asOf` | |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Missing create or edit on any write-path object | |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Bad `branchId`, or a target id not in this branch | |
| 409 | `CLAIM_REQUIRED` | A write targeted an inherited row | `claim` it first |
| 409 | `ALREADY_CLAIMED` | `claim` on a row this branch already owns | Edit it directly |
| 409 | `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | `exclude` on a tombstoned row | `restore` it first |
| 409 | `ALREADY_PRESENT` | `add` of a pair the branch already carries locally; or an op on a **replaced** row | Edit the existing row; or act on the substitute |
| 409 | `NO_OVERRIDE` | `restore` / `revert` / `convert-to-native` on a row the branch asserts nothing about | Nothing to undo |
| 409 | `NOT_SUPPLIED` | `revert` on a row no source supplies | `exclude` instead |
| 409 | `STALE_REVISION` | `update` against a revision superseded since your view | Reload and retry |
| 409 | `NOT_EDITABLE` | Target is inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly | Only source-supplied content is editable |
| 413 | `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` | More than 200 operations | Split the change |
| 422 | `CYCLE_DETECTED` | The edge would make a child an ancestor of its own parent | |
| 422 | `PARENT_NOT_IN_BRANCH` | `add` targeted a parent not in this configuration | |
| 422 | `EBOM_CYCLE` | The source eBOM already contains a cycle | |
| 422 | `UNSUPPORTED_CI_TYPE` | A delta named a non-structural CI | |
| 422 | `PROVENANCE_INVALID` | A delta named a source that is not this branch's | |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure | |

## Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | String(80) | No | — | `Baseline__c.Name`. Over 80 characters is a 400, not a 500 |
| `cutDateTime` | ISO-8601 | No | now | What to resolve against. **Never accepted in the future** |

> The request keeps the original caller-facing name `cutDateTime`; the **response** returns the two timestamps that name splits into.

## Two timestamps, and why they are not one

| Response field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resolutionTimePoint` | what the content was resolved at — stamped once, never re-derived |
| `takenAt` | the wall-clock moment of the cut |

Kept apart, a correction to the server clock cannot change what a baseline resolves to.

The timepoint is taken back **off the resolved snapshot** rather than computed separately, so the baseline is stamped with the clock the content was actually resolved at — not one a few milliseconds away.

## `memberCount` is not the tree row count

**Excluded rows are not members.** A tree read renders a tombstone so the editor can see what was removed; a baseline is the record of what the branch *contained*. The baseline read filters on the same predicate, so the stored count stays comparable to a later read — which is what makes it usable as a drift canary.

## Watch out for

- **Immutable from the insert.** There is no draft-baseline state and no lock step: every update to a `Baseline__c` is refused outright, and so is every hard delete.
- **Cutting changes future `update` behaviour.** The freeze means subsequent updates fork rather than revise in place, and come back `forked: true`.
- **A future `cutDateTime` is refused** — a baseline of content that does not exist yet is not a baseline.
- **201, not 200.** This call names one new resource, where a delta batch reports on a set of operations.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Baseline__c`, and **edit** on `Baseline__c` and `CI_Rev__c` (the freeze). Named separately because a partial grant would otherwise fail half way through the cut — after the members resolve and before the freeze, the one state a baseline must never be left in.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Unreadable body, or an over-length `label` |
| 400 | `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` | `cutDateTime` is later than now |
| 400 | `ASOF_INVALID` | `cutDateTime` could not be parsed |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Missing create or edit on `Baseline__c`, or edit on `CI_Rev__c` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Bad `branchId` |
| 422 | `EBOM_CYCLE` | The source eBOM contains a cycle, so nothing can be resolved to cut |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

request.description:
Re-resolves the branch at the baseline's stored `resolutionTimePoint` and returns the rows.

## Parameters

| Parameter | In | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `baselineId` | path | **Yes** | The `Baseline__c` |
| `flat` | query | No | Default `true`. **Honoured**, because a shape is not a clock |
| `asOf` | query | — | **Refused.** See below |

## `asOf` is refused, not ignored

Every other tree read on this API takes one, and a client that has been sending it to `/branches/{id}/tree` will send it here. A baseline **pins its own timepoint**, so a second one has nothing to answer — accepting it would give the same rows for every value and let a caller believe they had asked a temporal question and got a temporal answer. It is a **400 `INVALID_REQUEST`**.

## Differences from the branch read

| | Branch tree | Baseline tree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Excluded rows | **rendered**, `isExcluded: true` | **filtered out** |
| `edgeId` / `edgeKey` | populated | **suppressed** |
| `governingTimestamp` | populated | **suppressed** |
| `isReplaced` | populated | **populated** — a null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one |
| `MIXED_REVISION` warnings | forwarded | **not** forwarded |

A baseline row does not pretend to answer questions it cannot. Mixed-revision advice is about a branch someone is still editing; a baseline is a record of a decision already taken, so forwarding it would be answering a question nobody can act on any more.

## The two drift canaries

| warningCode | What moved |
| --- | --- |
| `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` | the baseline re-derived a **different number of rows** than its cut recorded — a corrected release date, an edit to an already-released BOM |
| `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` | the same row count, but a **different number of `claimed` rows** — the signature of a `convert-to-native` flipping a row from `claimed` to `local` after the fact |

Two canaries rather than one because **neither can see the other's drift**: a conversion leaves the row count, the quantities and the revisions all unchanged, so the first canary would report nothing while the baseline retroactively told a different story about which rows the branch had taken over.

Both **warn rather than throw**. The rows returned are still the honest answer for the stored timepoint, and refusing to answer would be worse than answering with a caveat.

## Watch out for

- **An empty baseline is a `200` with `rows: []`**, not an error.
- **Seeing drift is not a failure.** It is the system telling you something upstream moved — investigate the cause, do not re-cut reflexively.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | `asOf` was supplied |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | No read on `Baseline__c` or `Branch__c` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The baseline does not exist or is not visible |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

item.description:
Freezing and replaying a configuration.

**A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows.** The cut records one timestamp; reading it **re-resolves** the branch at that timestamp. That is exact, because the resolution is a pure function of the timestamp and because nothing can ever land at or *before* a past T — every acceptance and every delta is stamped with the wall clock as it is written.

The flattened member table this replaces cost one record per edge per cut — roughly **36 MB** at the measured 18,000-edge ceiling, and 100+ MB at Phase 2's target.

## What makes the replay honest, and it is not free

A `Draft` revision is edited **in place** by `update`, so re-resolving would follow an edit made *after* the cut and the baseline would change without anyone touching it. The cut therefore **freezes** every revision the snapshot resolved to. From then on every `update` to those rows forks a new revision instead — which is why `forked` starts coming back `true` after your first baseline.

request.description:
Computes the full effect of accepting a newer released revision of the branch's eBOM source — **before anything is written**. This is the review step a user sees prior to committing a pull.

**This call is pure.** It creates and modifies nothing. Calling it twice with the same inputs against an unchanged org returns identical output, **including identical `entryId` values**.

**Not every entry is a decision.** Most are informational: you are being told what will happen, not asked. Only `override-orphaned` blocks a commit.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceId` | Id | **Yes** | The `Branch_Source_CI__c` to pull from |

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `candidateRootRevisionId` | Id | No | latest released | The released revision to preview accepting. Must belong to the **same root item** the source already references, must be Released (not Cancelled or Expired), and must not resolve at or earlier than the source's current T_R |
| `entriesLimit` | Integer | No | 200 | Caps **informational** entries. Must be a positive integer — a present-but-unusable value is a 400 rather than a silent fallback |

## Response fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hasChanges` | `false` when the branch already resolves against the newest released revision. **Returns 200, not an error** |
| `currentSourceVersion` / `candidateSourceVersion` | `resolutionTimestamp` (T_R, stamped at acceptance and read forever after) is deliberately separate from `acceptedAt` (wall clock). Both `sourceRevisionId` and `acceptedAt` are **null on the candidate** — nothing has been accepted yet |
| `summary` | Counts by decision class and by kind, over the **untruncated** entry set |
| `entries[]` | Every difference. Each carries `current` / `candidate` state and a `detail` object holding the MBOM-specific fields |
| `warnings[]` | Typically `MIXED_REVISION` about what would render **after** the pull |
| `truncated` | `true` when the informational set was capped |
| `entriesLimit` | The effective cap applied this call |
| `diffFingerprint` | Opaque `sha256:` digest of the inputs + the **complete** entry set. Pass it back on commit |
| `generatedAt` | Server clock. Informational; **not** a resolution input, and **not** part of the fingerprint |

### Fields that are `null` rather than defaulted

| Field | Present on | Why null elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retargeted` | `override-retained` only | A `false` would assert something about a kind for which the question is meaningless |
| `overrideKind` | `override-*` kinds only | Same reasoning |
| `current` | — | Null for `member-added` — there is nothing there today |
| `candidate` | — | Null for `member-removed`, and for an orphan resolved by `remove` |

## Truncation

`entriesLimit` caps **informational** entries. **`required` entries are never truncated** — they block the commit, so hiding one would silently conceal a blocker. It is not a positional slice: a required entry past the cap is kept along with the service's own ordering.

`summary` always reports the **untruncated** totals, and `diffFingerprint` always covers the **complete** diff — so a truncated response is still safe to commit from.

This call is pure and deterministic, so retrieving more needs **no cursor**: re-issue with a larger `entriesLimit` and get back a longer, stable prefix of the same diff.

## Watch out for

- **This is a review step, not a mutation.** Nothing advances until you `POST .../pull`.
- **Already current is not an error.** A preview on an up-to-date branch returns `200` with `hasChanges: false` and an empty `entries` array — correct for a read, where the equivalent write throws.
- **Entry ids are opaque.** Stable across recomputation of the same diff, but **must not be parsed** — they are not database ids, and nothing has been created.
- **A cycle is a 422, not a 409.** A cycle is still a cycle no matter how many times you retry.
- **Gated on write, not read.** A read-only user is rejected before a pull is even previewed — the same grant `pull` itself requires. It is `assertUpdatable` on `Branch_Source_CI__c`, not `assertReadable` like the `tree` endpoint.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | `entriesLimit` was not a positive integer |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | No **write** access on `Branch_Source_CI__c` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Source, or `candidateRootRevisionId`, does not exist |
| 409 | `NOT_RELEASED` | Candidate is not Released, or is Cancelled, Expired, or missing a release date |
| 409 | `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER` | Candidate resolves at or before the source's current T_R |
| 422 | `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH` | Candidate belongs to a different root item than the source |
| 422 | `CYCLE_DETECTED` / `EBOM_CYCLE` | The eBOM below the candidate root contains a cycle |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

request.description:
Commits a previewed pull: appends a new acceptance advancing **T_R**, advances the source's root pointer, and applies your `override-orphaned` dispositions — **all under one savepoint**.

Returns **`201 Created`**, not 200: a new `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c` genuinely exists.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceId` | Id | **Yes** | The `Branch_Source_CI__c` to pull from |

## Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `candidateRootRevisionId` | Id | **Yes** | The released root revision being accepted |
| `diffFingerprint` | String | **Yes** | Echoed from the preview this commit is acting on |
| `decisions` | Array | No | `{ entryId, action }` pairs. **Every `override-orphaned` entry must appear** |

## The diff is re-resolved server-side

This endpoint **never trusts a client-held preview** — the eBOM or the branch may have changed since. It re-resolves the same diff through the same code path and answers `STALE_REVISION` the moment the re-resolved `diffFingerprint` disagrees with what you echoed back, or an `entryId` in `decisions[]` no longer names an entry in it.

A useful side effect: every preview-time failure mode (`NOT_RELEASED`, `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH`, `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, `NOT_FOUND`) applies here for free — nothing in the commit path re-implements them.

## Decisions

| Entry kind | Action | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `override-orphaned` | `convert-to-native` | Severs the provenance link, keeps the branch-owned content; it then resolves on the **branch** clock. Runs through the ordinary `convert-to-native` delta operation, so every invariant that batch enforces applies unchanged |
| `override-orphaned` | `remove` | Appends an **exclude** delta. **Nothing is hard-deleted** |
| Any other kind | *(none)* | No action exists — it applies automatically. A `decisions[]` entry naming one is rejected `INVALID_REQUEST` |

An `override-orphaned` entry with **no** decision blocks the commit with `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED`. There is **no default-accept tier** to fall back to.

## Override reconciliation — reported, never persisted

For every existing claimed or replaced field, the commit compares the override's current value against what the candidate traversal would natively produce:

- **Differs** → **reaffirmed** (`override-retained`). It stays active and continues to govern future pulls. **Nothing new is persisted** — the comparison is reconstructed from the accepted source version on every pull, so a "reaffirmation" record would change no rendered value.
- **Matches** → reported as **superseded** (`override-superseded`), never deleted, never written. From then on the field resolves like ordinary inherited content. Retiring it would mean a branch that once happened to agree with upstream would **silently start accepting** upstream changes from then on.

## Watch out for

- **All-or-nothing.** One outer savepoint around both the disposition batch and the acceptance insert. A failure part way leaves the prior accepted revision and T_R in place, with no orphaned claim, exclude or override-status records.
- **Stale previews are rejected.** Re-preview and resubmit — do not retry the same body.
- **Committed source revisions are immutable.** The new acceptance is an **insert**; a later update to one is refused outright.
- **Native content is untouched.** Branch-owned content with no upstream provenance is entirely unaffected by a pull.
- **`Edge_Key__c` / `Alias__c` are never re-stamped.** They keep meaning "the upstream line this edge was originally minted against", independent of the correlation key a pull actually joins on.
- **Committing the revision already accepted still succeeds.** It appends a new acceptance (advancing `acceptedAt` with the same T_R) and returns `applied: []` — the same reading the preview takes of the read side.
- **A re-preview immediately after a commit is always `hasChanges: false`.** That is why `applied[]` echoes the retained and superseded outcomes too: it is the only place to learn them.

## Access

Gated **before the body is read**, on both create and edit. Requires **create** on `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c`, `Branch_Member__c`, `CI__c`, `CI_Rev__c`, `Assembly_CI__c`, `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`; **edit** on `Branch_Source_CI__c`, `Assembly_CI__c`, `CI_Rev__c`.

## Error responses

| Status | code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Unreadable body; a decision names an entry that is not `override-orphaned`; unrecognised `action` |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Missing create or edit on any commit-path object |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Source, or candidate revision, does not exist |
| 409 | `STALE_REVISION` | `diffFingerprint` mismatch, or a stale `entryId` |
| 409 | `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` | An `override-orphaned` entry has no decision |
| 409 | `NOT_RELEASED` / `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER` | Revalidated at commit time and no longer qualifies |
| 422 | `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH` / `CYCLE_DETECTED` | Impossible against the model |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unmodelled server failure |

item.description:
Reconciling an MBOM branch against a newer version of the eBOM it inherits from. A **two-step** flow:

1. `GET .../pull-preview` — compute the diff, decide nothing, **write nothing**
2. `POST .../pull` — commit, supplying decisions for anything that needs one

---

# The correlation key — why a pull doesn't orphan every claim on every release

The two traversals are correlated on **`(Parent_Item__c, Item__c, Secondary_Unique_Key__c)`** — the legacy `Assembly__c.Tree_Unique__c` with the parent *revision* swapped for the parent *item*. **Not** on `Assembly_CI__c.Edge_Key__c`.

This is the load-bearing decision of the whole feature. When a parent item revs, Propel **clones its entire BOM into new `Assembly__c` rows with new ids** — so a branch that claimed a line under rev-1 holds a line id that does not exist under rev-2. A join on `Edge_Key__c` would orphan every claimed edge and re-add every upstream line **on every single pull**.

The parent *item* does not move when its revision does, which is exactly what lets this key survive the clone. `Edge_Key__c` still identifies the edge **for display**; it just is not the join key.

`Secondary_Unique_Key__c` rather than `Find_Number__c` because find-number uniqueness is org *configuration*, and a key built on it would give two orgs with identical data different diffs. Any two lines sharing (parent revision, child item) necessarily carry distinct secondary keys — a duplicate without one cannot physically be inserted.

# The two sides are deliberately asymmetric

| Side | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **current** | the branch resolved at the accepted T_R, **with** its own deltas overlaid |
| **candidate** | the **raw** upstream walk at the candidate T_R, with **no overlay at all** |

Overlaying the branch onto the candidate side would match nothing — the deltas are keyed on line ids that do not exist under the new root — and would append every delta as an unmatched *local* edge. That costs a third full traversal for values identical to the raw walk's, and worse: **it resurrects the orphans**. A claim on a line the candidate removed would come back as a local edge with the same parent and child items, correlate with the branch's own edge, land in `matched`, and `override-orphaned` would never be raised.

That entry is the **only** required decision in the entire feature. Silently losing it would make a commit that should block succeed.

# Entry kinds

| kind | decision | availableActions | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source-version-advance` | informational | — | The root item revision advances; nothing structural beneath it changed |
| `member-version-advance` | informational | — | An edge's child resolves to a newer released revision because T_R moved |
| `member-added` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge the branch has no native edge on. Enters automatically |
| `member-removed` | informational | — | The candidate removes an edge the branch never claimed or replaced. Applies automatically |
| `override-retained` | informational | — | The branch's override still differs from upstream; the branch wins and upstream is suppressed |
| `override-superseded` | informational | — | The branch's override now *matches* what the candidate would natively produce |
| `override-orphaned` | **required** | `convert-to-native`, `remove` | The candidate removes an edge the branch **claimed or replaced**. **Blocks the commit** |
| `member-add-collision` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge whose correlation key coincides with a branch-**native** edge. The branch's content wins automatically |

## Why a revision advance is never a decision

A revision is **not an independently assertable value**. Once you accept that the *line* exists, which revision it resolves to is a deterministic output of the as-of traversal against T_R — there is no alternative to offer. The only way to freeze a revision is `claim`, a separate and heavier operation that takes ownership of the whole edge.

## Why upstream re-pointing an edge at a *different item* is two entries

The correlation key includes the child item, so that never correlates as one matched pair. It decomposes into an independent `member-removed` (or `override-orphaned`) and an independent `member-added`.

So **`retargeted: true` means a different child *revision*, not a different child item.**

The complete REST surface of Propel's **Manufacturing BOM (MBOM)**, built on the new **branch / baseline / configuration-item** framework. Eight endpoints cover the whole lifecycle: create an MBOM over a released eBOM revision, read its structure, edit it with delta operations, freeze it as a baseline, and reconcile it against a newer eBOM revision.

The folders below are ordered as you would actually use them. Requests **chain**: each one saves the ids it creates into collection variables, so you can run them top to bottom against a fresh org without copying ids by hand.

---

# Read this first: the eight ideas the whole API rests on

## 1. An MBOM inherits its structure. It never copies it.

Creating an MBOM writes **four records and not one row of BOM structure**. The branch stores only its own *deltas*; everything else is resolved at read time by walking the live legacy `Assembly__c` graph beneath the accepted eBOM root revision. An untouched branch holds zero per-edge records however many times it is read.

## 2. `T_R` — the pinned source clock

When an MBOM is created (or a pull is committed), the accepted root revision's **release date** is stamped once as `Source_TimePoint__c`. That timestamp is **T_R**, and every inherited row resolves against it: a child item renders at whichever revision was released as of T_R.

T_R is *stamped, then read* — never re-derived. So when engineering releases `Assy-100` rev-2, **nothing happens to the MBOM**. It still resolves against rev-1's T_R until someone explicitly accepts the newer revision with a **pull**.

## 3. `asOf` — the branch clock, and why there are two

Every read also takes an `asOf` timestamp (defaulting to now). That one governs the *branch's* own content — its deltas, its locally added parts, its substitutes.

Two clocks are therefore legitimately in play at once, and every row states which one governs it:

| Row kind | Governing clock |
| --- | --- |
| `inherited` — supplied by the source, untouched | **T_R** |
| `claimed` — the branch took copy-on-write ownership | **T_R** for the child revision it pins |
| `local` — branch-owned, no upstream provenance | **`asOf`** |
| a *substitute* (from `replace`) | **`asOf`** — its child floats |

A direct consequence is that **one item can render at two different revisions in the same tree**. That is expected, not a fault, and comes back as a `MIXED_REVISION` warning beside the data rather than an error instead of it.

## 4. Provenance: `inherited` / `claimed` / `local`

Derived at read time, never stored. `claimed` and `local` differ by exactly one field on the winning delta row (`Overrides_Source__c` set vs. null), and that difference is what makes "what did I change relative to upstream?" answerable.

## 5. Copy-on-write: you must `claim` before you can edit

An inherited row is read-only. Editing it is refused with `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, carrying the eBOM line id so the client can offer the claim. Divergence from upstream is always an explicit act — an update that quietly claimed would make "what did I change?" depend on which fields a user happened to touch.

## 6. Nothing is ever deleted

Removal is an **exclude delta** — a tombstone appended to an append-only log. `restore` lifts it. A hard delete of any branch-owned row is refused (`HARD_DELETE_BLOCKED`). This is what makes a read at a past `asOf`, and therefore a baseline, reproducible.

## 7. A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

Cutting a baseline records one timestamp and freezes the revisions it resolved to. Reading it **re-resolves** the branch at that timestamp. Two stored counts act as canaries (`BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT`, `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT`) if something the resolution depends on has moved since.

## 8. "Pull", not "merge"

A pull is the **downstream-initiated acceptance of a newer upstream source version**, matching `Branch_Source_CI__c.Source_Type__c`. The word *merge* is deliberately reserved for the Phase 2 branch-to-branch operation, which is bidirectional and common-ancestor-based — genuinely different.

---

# Response and error conventions

The MBOM API does **not** use the Propel framework's `RestResponseHandler`. Each route serialises directly onto the HTTP response, so:

- Success and error bodies are **plain JSON, never wrapped** in the framework's `entity` / `entities` envelope.
- **Error bodies key the code as `code`, not `errorCode`.** `errorCode` is the framework's key; it appears in this API only *inside* a delta batch's per-operation `results[]`.
- **Nulls are not suppressed.** A field a producer never set is genuinely absent or explicitly `null`, and the two are meaningful — see `forked` on a delta result.
- `code` values come from a fixed enum. **The code is the contract; the message is not.** Messages are Custom Labels and are translated — switch on `code`, never on text.

## Status-code scheme

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **400** | The request could not be read, or a value is out of range. Fix the request. |
| **403** | No permission. The body carries the label only — never the object that was denied, because naming it would hand the caller the schema they were just refused. |
| **404** | The path, or an id in the body, names nothing. |
| **409** | Well formed, and **retryable after changing state** — claim it first, restore it first, re-preview. |
| **413** | More than 200 operations in one delta batch. |
| **422** | Well formed, but **impossible against the model**. Retrying unchanged will never succeed (a cycle is still a cycle). |
| **500** | Unmodelled server failure. Carries the exception type and message, never the stack trace. |

The 409/422 split is deliberate: a client that retries on a generic 4xx would spin forever on a cycle, and the two cases want different UI.

---

# Design intent: MBOM-specific paths, generic vocabulary

MBOM is the first application of a general branch / baseline / configuration-item framework. The `mbom` path segment exists to give MBOM-only rules somewhere to live, but the nouns below it — **branch**, **source**, **member**, **override**, **baseline** — are framework concepts, not MBOM concepts. All MBOM-specific data is confined to one `detail` object keyed by `ciType`. A future configuration-item type adds a sibling `detail` shape and changes nothing else.

# No `branchId` on the source endpoints

A source already names its owning branch (`Branch_Source_CI__c.Downstream_Branch__c`), so `/sources/...` paths take only `sourceId`. `branchId` still appears in the pull-preview response *body*, denormalised for display.

# Routing and namespace

These route through the existing `EntryAPI` → `EntryRoute` → `MbomRoute` framework (`src/main/default/classes/api/`), **not** a standalone `@RestResource`. In a package org the full path carries the namespace: `/services/apexrest/ksplm/api/v4/mbom/...`. In an unmanaged scratch/dev org there is no namespace segment.

---

# Setup

| Variable | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `propelApiUrl` | `{{endpoint}}/services/apexrest/{{namespace}}/api` | Add this as a **collection** variable if it is not already there — the existing v4 Design Hub requests reference it but it is not defined in the shared collection, so it renders as an unresolved placeholder in published docs for anyone who has not set it in a personal environment. |
| `mbomRootItemRevisionId` | a released `Item_Revision__c` id | The only value you must supply by hand. Everything else is captured from responses. |

Authorization is a standard Salesforce OAuth 2.0 access token / session id as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, inherited from the parent collection.
